title: shared-shadow-demultiplexer-credit-slicer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a production-safe way to duplicate a subset of live traffic to candidate model variants (canary/A/B) while enforcing per-tenant budgets, strict tenant isolation for replicas, and minimal latency impact for primary requests. Existing mirror implementations either lack fine-grained cost accounting or run shadow replicas in the same network namespace, increasing blast radius.

Goal: Implement a new shadowing pipeline ("shared shadow demultiplexer with credit slicing") that: 1) duplicates requests non-blockingly; 2) enforces per-tenant credit budgets and global spend caps; 3) supports adaptive sampling (watermark-driven and latency-aware); 4) runs shadow replicas behind ephemeral sandbox proxies for isolation; 5) emits billing-grade telemetry and trace linkage; 6) integrates with canary rollout controller and auto-rollback signals.
design_notes: Demultiplexer runs at the API gateway level: single pass decides shadow targets and sampling decisions to avoid double-costing downstream.
Credit Slicer: per-tenant budget tokens minted hourly. Sampling decisions consume tokens atomically; if tokens exhausted, shadow requests are skipped but logged for auditing.

Sampling strategy: hybrid watermark + PID controller. Watermark to guarantee minimum sample per tenant (for coverage), PID controller to maintain overall replica cost within target budgets by adjusting sample-rate continuum.
Isolation: shadow requests proxied to sandbox sidecars that enforce network egress/ingress rules and mount no persistent data. Sidecars run in dedicated sandbox pool (separate tenant quotas).

Failure modes: demultiplexer must be non-blocking; any downstream shadow failure cannot affect primary response. Timeouts for shadow requests are low (100ms) and failures are retried only in controlled replay jobs, not in-line.

Telemetry: every shadowed request stamped with a unique shadow_id and linked to primary request trace. Billing tags include tenant_id, model_variant, kernel_profile, token_estimate_at_time_of-decision.

Auto-rollback signals: if candidate model generates >5% error-rate regression or increases tail-latency beyond SLA by >25% for 3 consecutive 10-minute windows, the rollout controller triggers automatic demotion/rollback and notifies SRE/PM.

Cost accounting: we emit pre-estimated token counts for each shadow request using fast heuristic before dispatch (cheap), and reconcile with observed token usage in offline batch to adjust future budget forecasts.
Trade-off: stronger isolation increases operational cost (sandbox pool) but reduces blast radius for misbehaving models; opted for separation for enterprise customers with high security needs.
Privacy: payload redaction hooks are applied to shadow traffic (PII filters) before forwarding; redaction level configurable per-tenant and must be honored by sandbox proxies.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline duplicates live traffic to shadow variants without increasing tail latency for primary requests by >2ms on p99 in staging.
Per-tenant credit slicing enforces hourly budget and emits budget-usage metrics; if budget=0, no in-line shadowing occurs and a 'skipped_shadow' telemetry event is emitted.
Sandboxed sidecars successfully isolate network and file system access; security scans show no mount or host network leaks in canary runs.
Sampling controller keeps global shadow spend within configured bound (default 2% of total spend) under synthetic burst tests.
Auto-rollback triggers when defined regression thresholds are breached and rollback action is observed in rollout controller logs.
End-to-end trace linking present (primary_request_id -> shadow_id) in telemetry and usable by the Console for regression debugging.
Documentation and runbook exist and have been reviewed by SRE and Product (doc links attached).
Integration tests and chaos tests executed in staging demonstrating non-blocking behavior under 2x production traffic without any primary request failures caused by shadowing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for demultiplexer decision logic (sampling, token accounting, target selection).
Integration test: gateway + sandbox proxies + candidate models in staging with synthetic tenants that simulate budget exhaustion, burst traffic, and model failures.
Load test: run 2x baseline RPS with shadowing enabled and measure p50/p95/p99 latency impact on primary route; must meet acceptance criteria.
Chaos tests: kill sandbox proxies mid-flight to ensure demultiplexer degrades gracefully and primary responses unaffected.
Telemetry validation: replay captured traces through analytics job to ensure shadow linkages are preserved and billing tags are accurate.
Security review: run static config scanner against sandbox sidecar policies and KMS integrations for logging redaction keys.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary staging): enable pipeline for internal tenants only; monitor telemetry for 72 hours.
Phase 1 (limited customers): enable for 5 low-risk tenants with strict budgets and manual oversight; monitor real-time dashboards and alerts for 7 days.
Phase 2 (gradual ramp): enable adaptive sampling globally but with conservative global spend cap (1%); incrementally increase to default (2%) based on observed cost and error rates.

Rollback: rollout controller receives signal and flips routing to stop duplicating to candidate model variants; shadow inference pool drained and sandbox sidecars drained; automated incident created for investigation.
Final: enable for all tenants with opt-out flag available in tenant settings and documentation.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: shadow.sample_rate_per_tenant, shadow.tokens_consumed_hourly, shadow.skipped_count, shadow.error_rate_by_variant, shadow_tail_latency_by_variant, shadow_budget_violation_count.
Dashboards: per-tenant budget view, global spend burn-down, and correlated primary vs. shadow latency/risk view in Console.
Alerts: p99 primary latency regression >2ms (critical), candidate error-rate delta >5% (P0), budget burn-rate crossing 90% of hourly allocation (P1).
Audit logs: record every decision (shadowed, skipped, reason) with actor and sampling weight for postmortem and billing reconciliation.
